label: prop:frobenius-s-classification
title: Frobenius S-eigenvalue classification of the 3-term mass formula
html:
Under the Frobenius--Hopf antipode S \colon \sigma \leftrightarrow \sigma^{-1} on the Hecke algebra H_n(R, q), the three log-functionals in the Wedderburn mass formula (Wedderburn mass formula) behave as follows: \Phi_2 and \Phi_3 carry the S-eigenvalues +1 and -1, and \Phi_1 is not an S-eigenvector; only its symmetrised projection \Phi_1^{+} = \tfrac12(\Phi_1 + \Phi_1 \circ S) is S-even:

See Table 1.

Together with the S-classification of every coefficient in the formula:

See Table 2.

Write \Phi_1 = \Phi_1^{+} + \Phi_1^{-} with \Phi_1^{-} = \tfrac12(\Phi_1 - \Phi_1 \circ S), which is S-odd. Term by term, the binding correction \alpha\bigl(\Phi_1 - 2[3]_q\,\Phi_2 + h_{\mathrm{A}}^2\,\Phi_3\bigr) decomposes as:

\begin{aligned}
\text{Term 1: } & \underbrace{1}_{+1} \cdot \bigl(\underbrace{\Phi_1^{+}}_{+1} + \underbrace{\Phi_1^{-}}_{-1}\bigr) & \text{(no \(S\)-eigenvalue)} \\
\text{Term 2: } & \underbrace{-2[3]_q}_{+1} \cdot \underbrace{\Phi_2}_{+1} = +1 & \text{(\(S\)-even)} \\
\text{Term 3: } & \underbrace{h_{\mathrm{A}}^2}_{+1} \cdot \underbrace{\Phi_3}_{-1} = -1 & \text{(\(S\)-odd)}
\end{aligned}

The S-odd part of the mass has two channels, \Phi_1^{-} and the chirality term h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \Phi_3:

  \mathfrak{m}(S(\beta)) - \mathfrak{m}(\beta)
  = -2\alpha\bigl(\Phi_1^{-}(\beta) + h_{\mathrm{A}}^2\,\Phi_3(\beta)\bigr).

The chirality term is the only S-odd channel exactly when \alpha\,\Phi_1^{-}(\beta) = 0, which does not hold in general. Consequently, any S-symmetric ansatz for the binding correction (such as the 2-term \alpha-blend \alpha V_{\mathrm{Frob}} + (1-\alpha) V_{\det}, when both summands are S-invariant) has vanishing S-difference, and reproduces the S-difference of the mass only where the two channels cancel, \Phi_1^{-}(\beta) + h_{\mathrm{A}}^2\,\Phi_3(\beta) = 0, regardless of the mixing parameter.
